content: This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to unintended pregnancy. It is essential to consult your doctor or pharmacist to determine if you should use additional reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). Otherwise, contact a poison control center without delay. For residents in the United States, the poison control hotline is 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, it is important to undergo regular laboratory and medical tests, including assessments of liver function, viral load, T-cell counts, triglycerides, cholesterol levels, and blood sugar. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Capsules should be stored in the refrigerator, away from light, and must not be frozen. If necessary, they may also be stored at room temperature, but they should be discarded after 30 days if kept at room temperature. Tablets should be stored at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing any form of this medication in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
